name: Buenos Aires
region: Buenos Aires, on the Río de la Plata
tagline: The Paris of South America: grand boulevards, sunlit cafés, tango, bookshops, steakhouses and neighbourhoods each with a distinct personality, staying up until dawn.
highlight: A slow dinner of grilled beef and Malbec in Palermo at 10pm, followed by a milonga where the dancers do not stop until dawn.
shortDescription: Argentina's capital: a city of European architecture and Latin passion, with Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta Cemetery, San Telmo, La Boca, Teatro Colón, tango and some of the best food and nightlife in the Americas.
metaDescription: A Buenos Aires travel guide: Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta Cemetery, San Telmo market, La Boca and Caminito, Teatro Colón, El Ateneo, tango, parrillas, football, neighbourhoods and a four-day plan.
nearestAirport: Ministro Pistarini, Ezeiza (EZE), about 45 minutes to 1 hour; Aeroparque (AEP) for domestic flights
knownFor: Tango, steak, cafés, bookshops, European architecture, nightlife

image.alt: The Obelisco monument in Buenos Aires at sunset with wide avenues around it

intro: Buenos Aires was founded in 1536 and refounded in 1580 on the shore of the wide Río de la Plata, and it grew rich in the late 19th and early 20th centuries on the export of beef and grain. Immigration from Italy, Spain and elsewhere shaped its population, and its architecture, with wide boulevards, French-style mansions and Italian-inspired cafés, earned it the name Paris of South America. It remains one of the world's great cultural cities.

The city is a patchwork of barrios, each with its own character: San Telmo, with its cobbled streets and antique markets; La Boca, with its brightly painted houses; Recoleta, with elegant mansions and its famous cemetery; Palermo, a large area of parks, cafés, boutiques and nightlife; and Puerto Madero, a redeveloped dock area of restaurants and modern towers. It is a walkable city, and one of the best in the world for wandering.

Tango is the soul of the city, but so are football, cafés, bookshops, and the parrilla, or steakhouse. Portenos, as the residents are called, live late, eat late and talk with passion, and a visit rewards those who adopt their rhythm. It has economic troubles and periodic strikes, but its energy is unmatched.

whyVisit.intro: Buenos Aires is the cultural and culinary capital of South America, and a city of endless variety.

points.title: Tango and music
points.text: Dance halls, shows, street performers and a thriving live music scene.

points.title: Superb food
points.text: Steak, empanadas, pasta, dulce de leche and Malbec, in parrillas and cafés.

points.title: Architecture and history
points.text: Belle Époque mansions, grand plazas and colourful neighbourhoods.

points.title: Bookshops and cafés
points.text: One of the world's great bookshop cultures, with historic cafés to match.

points.title: Nightlife
points.text: Bars, clubs and milongas open until dawn.

attractionsIntro: The city is best explored by neighbourhood, with time for cafés in between.

attractions.name: Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada

image.file: File:Puerto Madero, Casa Rosada, Plaza de Mayo 01.jpg
image.alt: The pink Casa Rosada presidential palace on Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires

attractions.text: The historic heart of the city, with the pink Casa Rosada, the Cabildo and the Metropolitan Cathedral. The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo still march here on Thursday afternoons.
attractions.tip: Visit in the morning, and see the Thursday march.

attractions.name: Recoleta Cemetery

image.alt: Ornate mausoleums lining the alleys of Recoleta Cemetery in Buenos Aires

attractions.text: A city of the dead, with ornate mausoleums lining narrow streets, and the family tomb of Eva Perón. It is one of the most atmospheric cemeteries in the world.
attractions.tip: Go in the morning, and look for the cats.

attractions.name: San Telmo and its Sunday market

image.file: File:San Telmo Market, Buenos Aires, Argentina.jpg
image.alt: Antique stalls at the San Telmo Sunday market in Buenos Aires

attractions.text: The oldest neighbourhood, with cobbled streets, colonial houses, tango bars and a large market of antiques and crafts on Sundays.
attractions.tip: Go early on a Sunday, and watch your bag.

attractions.name: La Boca and Caminito

image.alt: Brightly painted houses on the Caminito street in La Boca

attractions.text: A working-class port district with brightly painted houses, tango dancers and the football stadium La Bombonera. The tourist street, Caminito, is safe by day, but stay within it.
attractions.tip: Take a taxi to and from, and visit by day.

attractions.name: Teatro Colón

image.alt: The grand façade of the Teatro Colón opera house in Buenos Aires

attractions.text: One of the world's great opera houses, opened in 1908, with superb acoustics and a lavish interior. Tours and performances are available.
attractions.tip: Book a tour, or see a show.

attractions.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid

image.alt: The interior of El Ateneo Grand Splendid, a former theatre turned bookshop

attractions.text: A former 1919 theatre turned into a spectacular bookshop, with balconies, a painted ceiling and a café on the stage.

attractions.name: Puerto Madero

image.file: File:Puente de la Mujer de Puerto Madero - Noviembre 2018.jpg
image.alt: The white Puente de la Mujer pedestrian bridge in Puerto Madero

attractions.text: The redeveloped docks, with restaurants, the Puente de la Mujer, a pedestrian bridge by Santiago Calatrava, and the Costanera Sur ecological reserve.
attractions.tip: Walk or cycle in the evening.

thingsToDoIntro: Buenos Aires is about strolling, eating and staying up late.

thingsToDo.title: Go to a milonga

image.file: File:Buenos Aires - Tango dancers in Sunderland Club - 7078.jpg
image.alt: Tango dancers at a milonga in Buenos Aires

thingsToDo.text: A dance hall where locals dance tango. Many offer a beginner class first.
thingsToDo.tip: Try a class first, and watch the etiquette.

thingsToDo.title: Eat at a parrilla
thingsToDo.text: Order a mixed grill, provoleta and salad, and share.

thingsToDo.title: See a football match
thingsToDo.text: Boca Juniors and River Plate matches are legendary.

thingsToDo.title: Have coffee in a historic café
thingsToDo.text: Historic cafés such as Café Tortoni, opened in 1858, offer coffee, medialunas and atmosphere.
thingsToDo.tip: Go off-peak to avoid the queue.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Palermo
thingsToDo.text: Palermo Soho and Palermo Hollywood are full of boutiques, cafés and bars.

thingsToDo.title: Take a day trip to an estancia
thingsToDo.text: A day on a ranch near the city, with a barbecue, horse riding and folklore.

foodIntro: Buenos Aires eats late and well, with beef at the centre, along with Italian-inspired pasta and pizza.

foods.name: Beef at a parrilla
foods.text: Bife de chorizo, ojo de bife and vacío, grilled on wood and charcoal.
foods.whereToTry: Parrillas in Palermo and San Telmo.

foods.name: Empanadas
foods.text: Baked or fried pastries with beef, cheese or vegetables.

foods.name: Medialunas and coffee
foods.text: Sweet croissants with a cortado, the classic breakfast.

foods.name: Pizza and pasta
foods.text: Thick pizzas and homemade pasta, from Italian immigrants.

foods.name: Dulce de leche
foods.text: Milk caramel in pastries, alfajores, ice cream and flan.

foods.name: Malbec and Torrontés
foods.text: The country's wines, in bars and restaurants.

accommodation.intro: Choose Palermo for nightlife, Recoleta for elegance and San Telmo for atmosphere.

areas.name: Recoleta and Retiro
areas.text: Grand hotels near museums and parks.

areas.name: San Telmo and the centre
areas.text: Guesthouses and hostels in old houses.

options.text: Direct flights from North America, Europe and across South America.
options.detail: Use a pre-booked transfer or an official taxi.

options.text: Flights to Iguazu, Patagonia, Mendoza, Salta and Bariloche.
options.detail: It is close to the centre.

options.text: Fast ferries from Colonia and Montevideo arrive at the port.

Radio taxis, Cabify and Uber operate.

bestTime.headline: September–November and March–May
bestTime.summary: Buenos Aires has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, sticky summers and mild, damp winters.

seasons.text: Warm and sunny, with jacaranda blossom.
Hot and humid, and many locals leave town.
Cool and damp, but good for culture.

bestTime.avoid: January and February for the heat.

itinerary.title: Four days in Buenos Aires
itinerary.intro: The historic centre, the barrios, culture and a day out.

days.title: The centre
days.morning: Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada.

days.title: Day out
days.morning: A day at an estancia, or the Tigre Delta.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you enjoy the city safely.
tips: Keep phones and bags out of sight, particularly on buses, the subte and busy streets.
Use taxi apps or radio taxis, especially at night.
Eat dinner late. Restaurants open at 8 or 9pm.
Visit La Boca in the daytime, and stay in the tourist area.
Check strike announcements, which can affect transport.
Book Teatro Colón tours and popular restaurants in advance.
Carry small notes for taxis and tips.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Buenos Aires?
faq.a: Three or four days for the highlights, and more for day trips.
Generally yes, but petty theft is common. Keep valuables hidden and use taxi apps.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: September to November and March to May.

faq.q: Do I need to see a tango show?
faq.a: It is a highlight, but choose between a show and a milonga, depending on whether you want a spectacle or an authentic evening.
Prices are volatile, and it can be cheaper or dearer than expected. Food and wine are good value.

faq.q: Can I see Buenos Aires on a stopover?
faq.a: A day or two lets you see the centre, Recoleta and San Telmo.
